Helpers for code that drops the class

Source: R/vctrs.R
zu_ifelse.Rd

Base functions that build their result from the values without their class, such as ifelse() and vapply(), read a zuint vector's raw bits as numbers. These helpers do the same jobs and keep the type.

Usage

zu_ifelse(test, yes, no)

zu_vapply(X, FUN, FUN.VALUE, ...)

Arguments

test

A logical vector.

yes, no

Values for TRUE and FALSE, recycled to test.

X

A vector or list.

FUN

A function.

FUN.VALUE

A zuint vector of the length each result must have.

...

More arguments to FUN.

Value

A zuint vector.

Details

zu_ifelse() takes yes and no to their common type (see zu_common_type()) and is NA where test is. zu_vapply() calls FUN on each element of X and requires each result to have the length of FUN.VALUE, a zuint prototype such as int64(0); the results take its type.

Examples

x <- int64(c("-9223372036854775807", "5", NA))
zu_ifelse(x > 0L, x, int64(0))
#> <int64[3]>
#> [1]  0  5 NA
zu_vapply(1:3, function(i) uint64(2)^i, uint64(0))
#> <uint64[3]>
#> [1] 2 4 8
